data.title: Header
data.tagline: The top section of a page that introduces the site or page and often contains navigation
data.description: A Header usually holds the brand and the paths people need first, such as main navigation, search, or account access. It is broader than a Navbar, which is specifically the navigation portion.

distinctions.label: Navbar
distinctions.explanation: Header is the complete top page area and can include brand, search, and sign-in. Navbar is the portion dedicated to primary navigation.

use: Use a page header when the brand, primary navigation, and account controls need to stay together at the top.
Documentation and ecommerce sites often need Search in the header.
Design the mobile header separately: keep the brand and primary actions, and move secondary links into a menu.
Put temporary announcements above the header, and keep their purpose distinct from navigation.
avoid: Cram every navigation link and action into the header, making important actions hard to find.
Make a fixed header so tall that it obscures content while the user scrolls.
Omit both a brand marker and a link home, leaving users unsure which site they are on.
Treat the page header and Navbar as the same thing. Distinguish them by the top-level container and their navigation role .

lessonPractice.title: A desktop header contains brand, five navigation items, search, and login, but wraps to two lines on mobile. How should it adapt?

options.label: Keep brand and the key action, and move secondary navigation into a dismissible mobile menu
options.feedback: The header preserves identity and primary access, while prioritization avoids shrinking every control beyond usability.

options.label: Keep every entry and reduce type, gaps, and button height until they fit one line
options.feedback: It may fit, but readability and click accuracy decline, and no mobile information priority is established.

options.label: Hide the brand and home entry while keeping navigation, search, and login
options.feedback: Users lose the site identity and stable home path, leaving a basic header responsibility unmet.

data.agentPrompt: Prioritize the header: keep brand, primary navigation, search, and login on desktop; retain brand and the key action on mobile and move the rest into a dismissible menu. Verify focus, current-page state, and long labels.
